question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-1, 4],$ compute $P(0<   X <  3).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14270027/assets/e8a1e7972e4e4a543c2e774894f83ec38755e7b2145a5b301e44906affac9c15.svg)

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-1,4],$ so it has the following probability density function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14270027/assets/5ca4ceb0bed3882328dbfa8fb54eb9de948a53d66d9850b8d40781d19f50f4fc.svg)

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0<X<3) & =P(0<X<3) \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3-0}{5} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
